sentences.text: Asteriornis was a small, long-legged bird that inhabited coastal environments.
The holotype specimen — the specific fossil the species is based on — is estimated to have weighed around 394 grams.
It possessed a slightly downcurved and lightweight beak.
The leg bones were elongated and slender, resembling those of modern ground-dwelling birds.
The radius bone flattened and widened toward the wrist, featuring a large hooked bump.
The discoverers nicknamed Asteriornis the "Wonderchicken" due to its unique characteristics.
It exhibits physical traits of both galliforms, or chicken-like birds, and anseriforms, or duck-like birds.
The genus was described by Field and colleagues in 2020.
The fossil remains were found at the CBR-Romontbos quarry near Eben-Emael in Belgium.
Researchers infer that Asteriornis had a terrestrial lifestyle and a generalist diet, which may have helped it survive the extinction event.
Asteriornis is considered one of the oldest known birds definitively belonging to the group Neornithes, or modern birds.
Phylogenetic analyses place it near the base of the superorder Galloanserae, which includes chickens and ducks.
Some studies suggest Asteriornis might be a paleognath related to tinamous and lithornithids, though this classification has limited support.
Recent analyses in 2025 placed Asteriornis within Galloanserae as a stem-galliform, but researchers could not confirm a specific jaw feature previously thought to be present.
Asteriornis lived during the Late Maastrichtian stage of the Cretaceous period.
It lived approximately 66.8 to 66.7 million years ago.
The Maastricht Formation where the fossil was found is named after the final stage of the Cretaceous period.
The Paleobiology Database records the time range of Asteriornis as 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
